definitions.explanation: Not harmful or dangerous. Primarily used in medical contexts to describe tumors, growths, or conditions that are not cancerous or life-threatening.

examples.japanese: {良性|りょうせい}の{腫瘍|しゅよう}だった。
{検査|けんさ}の{結果|けっか}、{良性|りょうせい}と{判明|はんめい}した。
examples.english: The test results revealed it to be benign.

examples.japanese: {良性|りょうせい}のポリープでも{定期的|ていきてき}に{経過|けいか}{観察|かんさつ}が{必要|ひつよう}です。
examples.english: Even benign polyps require regular follow-up observation.

notes:
Composed of {良|りょう} (good) and {性|せい} (nature/character). Almost exclusively used in medical contexts. When hearing test results, {良性|りょうせい}です is reassuring news.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {良性|りょうせい}{腫瘍|しゅよう}: benign tumor
- {良性|りょうせい}のポリープ: benign polyp
- {良性|りょうせい}と{診断|しんだん}される: to be diagnosed as benign
- {良性|りょうせい}{疾患|しっかん}: benign disease

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {悪性|あくせい}: malignant — the opposite; cancerous or dangerous
- {陽性|ようせい}: positive (test result) — a different medical term; positive does not mean malignant
- {陰性|いんせい}: negative (test result) — negative test result

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
Do not confuse with {両性|りょうせい} (both sexes / bisexuality), which has the same reading.
